summary: Treating the 5-minute budget as a compute-allocation problem paid off with two constants and zero code changes: TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE 2**19 -> 2**18 (grad_accum 2->1) gave 0.997333 -> 0.988168, and widening ASPECT_RATIO 64 -> 96 (n_embd 512 -> 768, 6 heads, depth 8) gave a further 0.988168 -> 0.981817. Widening is cheaper than its FLOP count because MFU climbs with matmul size (38.5 -> 45.0%), so the model trains on fewer tokens but still wins. What did not work: batch 2**17 was worse than both 2**18 and the baseline (0.999011, MFU collapses to 32%); n_embd 1024 fell off a cliff (1.053934, only 726 steps -- badly undertrained); and depth 10 / n_embd 640 lost to depth 8 / n_embd 768 at matched FLOPs (0.986542), so extra compute belongs in width, not layers. Next I would probe the untested n_embd 896 (between the flat region and the cliff, needs DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE 64 for VRAM), re-tune MATRIX_LR and the warmdown fraction at the new 1091-step count since those were inherited from a ~918-step setting, and check whether MLP ratio 4x is still right at n_embd 768.
